title: Checkpointed streaming envelope and tool-idempotency acceptance criteria
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and accept concrete runtime and QA behaviors for progressive/streamed structured responses and deterministic tool/function call semantics. Primary goals: (1) establish a minimal but rigorous schema-handshake and versioning convention for streaming responses, (2) introduce checkpoint frames so partial outputs are verifiable and resumable, (3) codify tool-invocation idempotency tokens and retry semantics, and (4) define error envelope classes and backpressure signals with observability requirements. This ticket consolidates product requirements, acceptance criteria, test plan, and links to design/engineering artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Schema handshake: every streaming session MUST start with a single 'schema_handshake' frame that includes schema_id, schema_version, and 'mode' (partial|complete). If the client omits handshake, server must treat incoming stream as 'best-effort' untyped and emit a warning telemetry event.

Version compatibility: if schema_version is incompatible (major version mismatch), the service MUST emit an immediate 'schema_error' frame explaining compatibility and include 'fallback_suggestion' (string) with an allowed fallback schema_id if available.

Checkpoint frames: the runtime MUST support explicit 'checkpoint' frames at configurable token boundaries. Each checkpoint MUST include a checkpoint_id (UUID), byte_offset, and stable_hash of emitted partial object. Clients must be able to request resume from a checkpoint_id and receive a concise 'resume_ack' frame.

Partial object validity: any 'partial_object' frames MUST be syntactically valid JSON fragments that, when concatenated in checkpoint-delimited sequences, produce a syntactically valid object that validates against the declared schema at the handshake. Validation failures at checkpoint boundaries MUST emit a 'validation_error' frame with error_code and repair_hint.

Backpressure control frame: the runtime MUST support a control frame 'PAUSE' and 'RESUME' originating from client or server. When 'PAUSE' is received, the server must stop sending non-control token payloads within 50ms and emit 'paused_state' telemetry. Resume must continue from last checkpoint as per resume_ack behavior.

Tool invocation envelope: tool calls MUST be represented as dedicated 'tool_call' frames that include call_id, tool_name, args_schema_id, idempotency_token (client-provided or generated), and expected_response_schema_id. Tool frames must be delivered in-order relative to their logical invocation.

Tool-call idempotency and retries: when a client re-sends a tool_call with the same idempotency_token, the runtime MUST guarantee at-least-once semantics for delivery to the target tool but MUST expose deduplicated outcomes to the client. If tool is non-idempotent, service must return 'non_idempotent_tool' status during handshake or tool registry lookup and refuse automatic retries unless explicit 'force' flag is set by caller.

Partial tool responses: tools MAY stream their outputs back as 'tool_stream' frames. The platform must be able to interleave tool_stream frames with main-stream frames and maintain per-call call_id scoping. Finalization of a tool_call is signaled with 'tool_complete' frame including success boolean and a result_checksum.

Error envelope taxonomy: errors emitted in-stream MUST follow a 3-part envelope: {scope: (schema|tool|platform), code: short_string, message: human_readable, repair_hint: optional_string}. The 'scope' must allow automated routing of incidents to the correct owner (e.g., schema mismatches -> product; tool timeouts -> integrations).

Graceful degradation: when a streaming schema validation fails mid-stream but partial payloads are semantically useful, the runtime MUST continue emitting a 'degraded_mode' frame and tag subsequent outputs with 'validation_confidence' (high|medium|low). A final 'degradation_summary' frame must include the list of failed checks and suggested remediation steps.

Observable telemetry: the following events MUST be emitted for each stream: schema_handshake.{ok|incompatible}, checkpoint.emitted, checkpoint.resumed, validation_error, tool_call.{started|completed|failed|deduped}, backpressure.{pause|resume}, and degraded_mode.entered. Each event must include stream_id, user_id (if available), and latency_ms where applicable.

SLO guardrails: a streaming handshake and initial schema validation must complete in under 150ms p50 and 400ms p95. Checkpoint write latency for a typical 2k token chunk must be under 30ms p95 when running in hosted mode (no dedicated capacity).

End-to-end tests: there must be automated tests that verify: (a) resume from checkpoint after simulated network interruption preserves schema conformance, (b) idempotent tool_call deduplication returns a single effective action when the tool is flaky, (c) interleaved tool_stream and main-stream frames reorder resilience (out-of-order delivery reconstructed correctly), and (d) backpressure 'PAUSE' stops payload emission within 50ms in test harness.

Contract docs and examples: PRD must include at least three canonical examples: (1) long-running generator that emits progressive structured paragraphs with checkpoints, (2) a tool-calling flow where a payment tool is invoked and may return async events, demonstrating idempotency tokens, and (3) a schema-mismatch fallback where the client downgrades to 'untyped' mode after receiving 'schema_error' with suggested fallback.

Compatibility fallback: when a client requests 'strict' mode in the handshake, the server MUST refuse streams that cannot be validated at every checkpoint and respond with 'strict_reject' plus a machine-readable list of incompatible fields.
non_goals: Designing a general-purpose streaming database or long-term persisted stream store (this ticket only requires short-term checkpointing for resume across unstable client connections).
Defining per-customer custom schema negotiation flows beyond the public registry (those are future work).
open_questions: Should idempotency_token be required for every tool_call or only for calls flagged as potentially side-effecting?
Do we allow server-generated idempotency_tokens for convenience and surface them to clients in a 'call_token' field?
What rate of checkpointing is optimal by default for token-cost vs resume fidelity (configurable knob to be decided)?
How should RBAC affect exposure of tool names and schema_ids in handshake frames for Private deployments?

telemetry_requirements: Emit event stream_id and event_type with each telemetry event
Include schema_id and schema_version in handshake events
Record tool_name and call_id for tool_call lifecycle events
Expose validation_confidence and failed_check_count in degraded_mode events
test_plan: Unit tests for handshake parser (valid, missing fields, incompatible version)
Integration test: checkpoint -> simulate TCP drop -> resume with checkpoint_id -> validate object equality
Chaos test: interleaved out-of-order frames and verify reconstruct order by frame sequence and call_id
E2E test with a non-idempotent toy tool to verify platform refuses automatic retry without 'force' flag
